secondaryTitle: How I Launched My Online Business Against All Odds in Pakistan
raw:
My Journey to Launch Farhan Deals: Overcoming Bank Account Challenges for Online Business

Farhan Deals. The name itself has become a part of my identity, a brand remembered by many. It's my most significant, most famous, and certainly my favorite project and business. But its journey wasn't smooth from the start; there's an interesting story behind it, which I'm excited to share with you today.

This story begins in December 2025. Before that, I was constantly searching for what I could do online. Honestly, I had no idea how online work even functioned; it seemed almost impossible to me. However, my father, a ranger officer, always encouraged me to pursue freelancing and online work, urging me to earn my own money. Whenever he came home on weekends, he would take me out to look for institutes that taught online skills. But after wasting entire days, we'd find nothing. My father would get frustrated, asking why I didn't know where these institutes were. I'd listen to his lectures, feeling annoyed but staying silent, wondering how I could find something that simply wasn't there.

Before this, during one of my father's holidays, we chanced upon a place that taught Amazon e-commerce. I went with him, enrolled, and paid an advance fee of 5,000 rupees. I attended for one day. I remember a projector-like setup showing Amazon on a wall, and someone typing codes – perhaps country-specific codes that changed settings. It's an old memory, so I'm not entirely sure. But I didn't understand anything. I went for one day, then a second, then a third, and that was it. I told my father it was too advanced and I couldn't grasp it. The other students were much older than me, making me feel quite small. My father was upset. He went back to get the fees refunded, but they refused, offering instead to enroll me or someone else. So, we never got the money back.

Now, let's fast forward to December 2025, specifically the last 15 days of the month. One night, as I was scrolling through Reels, an ad popped up: 'Learn Shopify dropshipping for free, online, with guaranteed income.' I immediately contacted them on WhatsApp, and they sent a link to their WhatsApp channel. I joined, and they would share YouTube links for live classes from 8 to 9 PM. If I missed a live session, the full lecture was available on YouTube the next morning. I followed this routine, sometimes attending live, sometimes watching the uploaded videos.

They gave daily homework based on what they taught, like creating a Facebook page, connecting it to Instagram, building a portfolio, and finding products. The WhatsApp channel was a place for us all to share our progress and problems. For any issues, like how to create a portfolio, they provided a dedicated number for support. I even gave them access, and they helped set up my portfolio and ad settings. There were about 8 to 9 lectures in total, and I believe these videos are still available on a YouTube channel named Saad Bashir.

Towards the end of the lectures, they announced that they had taught us almost everything, and we should now be able to start on our own. However, for those who were still confused but wanted to launch, they offered a startup package for 15,000 rupees. This package included buying and setting up a custom domain, building a Shopify store, and running 2-3 test ads – essentially a complete startup setup. I chose this option.

As instructed, I sent 2,000 rupees after each step was completed, eventually sending a total of 10,000 rupees. The final 5,000 rupees were split: 2,000 for their services and 3,000 to be deposited into my bank account (Sadapay or Nayapay) for ad spending. But I didn't have a Nayapay, Sadapay, or any personal bank account. After much confusion, I remembered my mother's bank account. I tried to use it, but its international transactions were off. I kept trying to connect it, which unfortunately led to the account being permanently blocked.

By then, I had already paid 12,000 rupees, and my Shopify store, with a custom domain, was ready. My Instagram and Facebook accounts were connected for ads. All that remained was setting up the ads. The date was January 3, 2026. I was stressed, and the agency was pressing me to find a bank account to finalize the work. They kept extending the deadline, first to January 10, then to January 15.

I tried desperately to open a Sadapay account using my mother's CNIC, but there was an issue with face verification – perhaps a camera problem or something else. Eventually, I gave up on Sadapay. Then I tried Nayapay. Verification was difficult but eventually went through. However, I wasn't home when Nayapay called, and my mother, confused by the questions, inadvertently caused the account to be blocked. So, Nayapay didn't work either. Finally, I tried my father's bank account, but it also faced similar issues and got blocked.

It felt like I was hitting a wall every time for one reason or another. After many attempts, I finally gave up and told the agency, which was still owed 3,000 rupees, to just finish my work. I said I'd get a bank account later and set up the ads myself. The truth was, I didn't have my CNIC, so I couldn't open a bank account.

For a long time, I worried that my 12,000 rupees would go to waste if I couldn't run ads. Then, I remembered seeing my uncle's checkbook at home when I was a child. I searched for it and finally found it. I discussed it with my uncle, who told me the account hadn't been used for a long time and had been closed. I insisted he reactivate it, promising to cover all costs. We made several trips to the bank with my uncle, which took about a month. Finally, they confirmed the account was active, but I needed an ATM card. Registering and activating the ATM card took another month.

Finally, with the ATM card active, I was able to launch the ads successfully. Within 2-3 days, I even got 1-2 customers! That's how Farhan Deals truly began. To this day, I'm still using my uncle's bank account, as I'm not yet 18 and don't have my own. Today, November 12, 2026, I have submitted my CNIC verification, and it should be ready in a few days. After that, I'll apply for my own bank account.

This entire experience is the main reason I've kept my business somewhat limited. Even using my uncle's account has its difficulties: sometimes he's at work, sometimes there are verification issues, or suddenly the balance drops to zero, blocking active ads. These kinds of issues have been frequent. It proves that every task starts with difficulty, and things are rarely as easy as they seem. Unexpected difficulties always arise, ones we can't even imagine beforehand.

As of November 11, my Shopify store is currently closed to avoid fees. Shopify charges $1 for the first three months per store, then around $20 (I'm not entirely sure of the exact amount). So, I used one Gmail for three to four months, then switched to another Gmail for a new trial. Now, for the third time, I've closed the store and saved a copy of it. Currently, I'm doing e-commerce only through social accounts, without a dedicated website. You can still view my Shopify store at farhandeals.store by entering '1' as the password – it's not functional for shopping, but the copy is saved, which is good.

I'm living like this for now, waiting for my CNIC and then my own bank account, after which I plan to start my work professionally, Inshallah. I know it won't be as simple as I imagine, but I pray that it goes smoothly, Ameen.
